The same document indents equivalent sub-lists three spaces (e.g. page 395 rule 9) a)-c), page 411 rule 1) a)-c), page 415 rule 6) a)-b)), so this is a local transcription lapse, not the document convention.

verdict.reasoning: REFUTED as a content discrepancy: the difference is leading whitespace only, and it is not local. (1) Text fidelity is exact. I rendered p397 at 300 dpi and compared every item against the markdown slice. All eight sub-items are present, verbatim, in the correct a)-h) order, immediately after rule 24), with no omission, insertion, reordering, or wording change: a) Another level 88 entry. / b) A level 66 entry. / c) An alphanumeric group containing items with a usage other than display. / d) A group containing items described with a JUSTIFIED or SYNCHRONIZED clause. / e) A data item of the class index, message-tag, object, or pointer. / f) A data item described with the ANY LENGTH clause. / g) A type declaration described with the STRONG phrase, or a group item subordinate to such a type declaration. / h) A variable-length group. Rule 24)'s own body, including the 'except the following:' lead-in, also matches the print verbatim. (2) The 'misplaced-content' kind is a misnomer. Nothing is misplaced. The content sits in exactly the right place and sequence, scoped by the colon-terminated lead-in of the rule that immediately precedes it. Only the count of leading space characters differs (PDF indents to the rule's text column; markdown emits column 0). (3) No meaning is lost. The items carry their own a)-h) lettering while the enclosing syntax rules are numbered 22), 23), 24), so a lettered item can never be mistaken for a numbered sibling rule. A reader or a parser keying on the letter series plus 'except the following:' recovers the exact same scoping the print indentation conveys. Interpretation of rule 24 is unchanged. (4) The stated rationale is factually wrong on its central point. I confirmed the three cited comparators do use indent 3 (p395 rule 9) a)-c), p411 rule 1) a)-c) and rule 2) a)-c), p415 rule 6) a)-b)), but 'local transcription lapse' does not survive a document-wide count. Scanning every lettered sub-list that directly follows a colon-terminated numbered rule in specs/ISO_COBOL.md: 245 such groups on 199 pages are indented, and 81 groups on 65 pages are flush at column 0 (pages 82, 103, 160, 211, 255, 279, 304, 323-326, 331, 397, 401, 462, 464, 466, 476, 500, 528, 539, 549, 550, 600, 612, 617, 621, 642, 646, 670, 677-679, 684, 710, 711, 717, 730, 741, 743, ...). Page 397 is one instance of a recurring ~25% transcription pattern, not a defect peculiar to this page. This falls squarely under the exclusions for formatting-only differences that do not change meaning. If the owner ever wants uniform sub-list indentation, that is a single mechanical whitespace normalization across all 65 affected pages, not a page-397 spec-reconciliation finding, and it carries no semantic risk to the compiler.
